name: Should I Stay or Should I Go

podcast.body: Featured on The Clash's 1982 album *Combat Rock*, this song was inspired by Joe Strummer's then-girlfriend, Ellen Foley, who was also known for her role in Meat Loaf's song "Paradise by the Dashboard Light." The song's theme of indecision resonated with the internal struggles and tensions that were increasingly plaguing The Clash during this period.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Licensed for a Levi's jeans commercial in 1991, a decision made because the band members were "quite skint" and had not capitalized on their fame, six years after their breakup. The band had previously rejected offers from companies like Dr. Pepper and British Telecom. Mick Jones, the song's principal creator, approved the deal, reasoning that Levi's were "working class pants." The commercial, which aired on British TV, along with promotion for Jones's post-Clash project, Big Audio Dynamite, led to the song's reissue as a single, which subsequently reached number one in the UK, becoming The Clash's first and only number one hit. "The group punted the decision to Mick Jones, who was the principal creator of that song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This is the original version and Mick Jones mix of the song, which was intended for the unreleased *Rat Patrol from Fort Bragg* album. It later became a big single from *Combat Rock*. This version offers a chance to hear the difference compared to the widely known *Combat Rock* version. "One of the big singles from Combat Rock was Should I Stay Or Should I Go? This is the original version. Let's see if you can hear the difference with the one that we've heard all these years. The clash and the Mick Jones mix of Should I Stay Or Should I Go from a clash album that was destined to be released as Rat Patrol from Fort Bragg, but turned into Combat Rock in the end."

podcast.body: This song captures the uncertainty and questions surrounding Joe Strummer's eight-week disappearance in April and May of 1982, an event that retrospectively marked the beginning of the end for the band. "Now, should I stay or should I go now? If I could, I will be sure of all. And if I stay, it will be."

podcast.body: This song is listed by Spotify as the "11th most popular song played by surgeons while they operate." The lyrics of the song were quoted directly in the transcript in conjunction with this statistic. "Should I stay or should I go now? If I go there, we'll look trouble. If I stay, it will be trouble. So you gotta let me know. Should I stay or should I go? The 11th most popular song played by surgeons while they operate, according to Spotify."
